analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: Other sources checked
analysis_refs.text: | [Wikisource](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Main_page) | Public metadata APIs returned stable page IDs in English, Hindi and Tamil. | Resolve redirects, distinguish work/edition lists and transclusions from complete editions, preserve contributors and per-text rights. The sampled Hindi title redirected. Do not treat namespace 0 or HTTP 200 alone as a readable book. |

analysis_refs.heading: Other sources checked
analysis_refs.text:
The next strongest scholarly-book candidates are DOAB/OAPEN, followed by
Wikisource for multilingual editions. They remain researched candidates, not
enabled sources. No paid integration, new reader account or source outreach
was performed. Redis remains deferred for the four existing live paper adapters;
the book catalogs and source research are independent of that setup.

analysis_refs.heading: 2. Twenty categories and how to find candidates for each
analysis_refs.text: | C02 General books and ebooks | National-library digital catalogs, public-domain publisher directories, Wikisource community links, Gutenberg-related catalogs | National/state digital libraries, regional literature academies, university digitization projects, Tamil/Hindi and other language collections | Official metadata exports, OPDS or documented search; distinguish full books from scans of covers, previews and loans |

analysis_refs.heading: The ten candidates
analysis_refs.text: | 2 | [Wikisource](https://www.mediawiki.org/wiki/API:Search) | Literature and historical books; original-script Indian-language coverage | English mathematics-title query → **A History of Mathematics (1893)**; Tamil `திருக்குறள்` → **திருக்குறள், மூலம்** | MediaWiki search plus page/section resolution; EN/TA are one source candidate |

analysis_refs.heading: Reading evidence and source-specific limits
analysis_refs.text: | Wikisource | English introduction returned 18,376 characters of rendered HTML; Tamil **உழவு** section returned 7,337. Native page IDs and parent/section links resolved. | Search returns chapters, version pages and entire works together. Preserve language, edition, parent work, proofread status and applicable rights; do not label a contents page or incomplete transcription a complete book. |

analysis_refs.heading: Query behavior and operating constraints
analysis_refs.text:
Thoth publisher filters and active book types constrain results, but results are
not guaranteed to be ordered by reader relevance. They can match descriptions.
Wikisource needs whole-work/section handling. GDL needs token/phrase relevance
checks. These observations are particularly relevant to the earlier irrelevant
free-search results: a working API alone does not finish search quality.

analysis_refs.heading: Coverage and the next decision
analysis_refs.text:
If selected to advance later, prioritize GDL for children's coverage, Wikisource
for Indian-language literature, and the five Thoth publishers for shared
engineering. BHL and LoC add historical depth; LibriVox adds audio and requires an
appropriate listening-result design. Keep source qualification and new UI review
before implementation under the agreed workflow.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.
